page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top centre. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: terum vegetans,ut sunt omnes plantæ. Alterum eorum,quæ per se moventur,& sentiunt,ut cuncta animantia.

In omnibus autem naturalibus mistis perfectis quatuor prima mundi elementa(quæ revera, & secundùm naturam miscibilia sunt)cum suis primis qualitatibus mutua actione & passione ad unam,mediamq; reducuntur substantiam,comparantq; formam ab ipsis miscibilibus valde diversam: ita ut hæc non plura sint, sed unū per se. Quoniam autem elementa quatuor ad mistionem seipsa movere,neq; ad iusta consentanea q; cuiusque rei pondera ac mensuras confluere nequeunt:ideo motore aliquo indigent, atq; tali motore,qui convenience proportione cogat ipsa: deinde coacta misceat,atq; cõtem peret, ne quid videlicet,vel redundet,vel desit. Porrò vim illam cœlo tribuit Aristoteles libro primo de Generatione & Corruptione. Sed cùm cœlum (pace tanti philosophi dixerim) electione careat,nec miscibilia ad convenientem proportionem, mensuramq; reducere per se, & primo potens sit:idcirco id munus Deo omnipotenti primùm & præcipuè assignare convenit. Est enim summus & optimus,atq; etiam sa-
[The last line of the printed text reads "pientissi-" as catchword.]

page.notes: Words marked by the printer's ligature "ct" in "cuncta" and "conveniente" are read as printed. The line "sa-" at the end of the page is a split word whose remainder is the catchword "pientissi-". Long s is written plain throughout, u/v and i/j normalised. "motore" and "mensuras" read clearly; "cuncta" is slightly uncertain due to the ligature. The running head is set in small capitals and is copied as printed.
